label: Acts 13:1
text: Now in the assembly that was at Antioch there were some prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

label: Acts 13:2
text: As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.”

label: Acts 13:3
text: Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.

label: Acts 13:4
text: So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia. From there they sailed to Cyprus.

label: Acts 13:5
text: When they were at Salamis, they proclaimed God’s word in the Jewish synagogues. They had also John as their attendant.

label: Acts 13:6
text: When they had gone through the island to Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar Jesus,

label: Acts 13:7
text: who was with the proconsul, Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding. This man summoned Barnabas and Saul, and sought to hear the word of God.

label: Acts 13:8
text: But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.

label: Acts 13:9
text: But Saul, who is also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fastened his eyes on him,

label: Acts 13:10
text: and said, “Full of all deceit and all cunning, you son of the devil, you enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?

label: Acts 13:11
text:
Now, behold, the hand of the Lord is on you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a season!”
Immediately a mist and darkness fell on him. He went around seeking someone to lead him by the hand.

label: Acts 13:12
text: Then the proconsul, when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.

label: Acts 13:13
text: Now Paul and his company set sail from Paphos, and came to Perga in Pamphylia. John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.

label: Acts 13:14
text: But they, passing on from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia. They went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and sat down.

label: Acts 13:15
text: After the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, “Brothers, if you have any word of exhortation for the people, speak.”

label: Acts 13:16
text: Paul stood up, and beckoning with his hand said, “Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen.

label: Acts 13:17
text: The God of this people chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they stayed as aliens in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm, he led them out of it.

label: Acts 13:18
text: For a period of about forty years he put up with them in the wilderness.

label: Acts 13:19
text: When he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave them their land for an inheritance, for about four hundred fifty years.

label: Acts 13:20
text: After these things he gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.

label: Acts 13:21
text: Afterward they asked for a king, and God gave to them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.

label: Acts 13:22
text: When he had removed him, he raised up David to be their king, to whom he also testified, ‘I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who will do all my will.’

label: Acts 13:23
text: From this man’s offspring, God has brought salvation to Israel according to his promise,

label: Acts 13:24
text: before his coming, when John had first preached the baptism of repentance to Israel.

label: Acts 13:25
text: As John was fulfilling his course, he said, ‘What do you suppose that I am? I am not he. But behold, one comes after me, the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.’

label: Acts 13:26
text: Brothers, children of the stock of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, the word of this salvation is sent out to you.

label: Acts 13:27
text: For those who dwell in Jerusalem, and their rulers, because they didn’t know him, nor the voices of the prophets which are read every Sabbath, fulfilled them by condemning him.

label: Acts 13:28
text: Though they found no cause for death, they still asked Pilate to have him killed.

label: Acts 13:29
text: When they had fulfilled all things that were written about him, they took him down from the tree, and laid him in a tomb.

label: Acts 13:30
text: But God raised him from the dead,

label: Acts 13:31
text: and he was seen for many days by those who came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are his witnesses to the people.

label: Acts 13:32
text: We bring you good news of the promise made to the fathers,

label: Acts 13:33
text:
that God has fulfilled the same to us, their children, in that he raised up Jesus. As it is also written in the second psalm,
‘You are my Son.
Today I have become your father.’

variants.reading: εν τω πρωτω ψαλμω γεγραπται ('it is written in the FIRST Psalm') and εν τοις ψαλμοις γεγραπται ('it is written in Psalms')
variants.note: Fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles', Acts 13:33: the WEB order εν τω ψαλμω γεγραπται τω δευτερω is read by P75, א, A, B, C, Psi, 33...; D* reads 'first Psalm' and P45 'in Psalms'. Sinaiticus and Vaticanus carry the WEB reading (not the variant).

label: Acts 13:34
text: “Concerning that he raised him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he has spoken thus: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David.’

label: Acts 13:35
text: Therefore he says also in another psalm, ‘You will not allow your Holy One to see decay.’

label: Acts 13:36
text: For David, after he had in his own generation served the counsel of God, fell asleep, and was laid with his fathers, and saw decay.

label: Acts 13:37
text: But he whom God raised up saw no decay.

label: Acts 13:38
text: Be it known to you therefore, brothers, that through this man is proclaimed to you remission of sins,

label: Acts 13:39
text: and by him everyone who believes is justified from all things, from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.

label: Acts 13:40
text: Beware therefore, lest that come on you which is spoken in the prophets:

label: Acts 13:41
Acts 13:42
text: So when the Jews went out of the synagogue, the Gentiles begged that these words might be preached to them the next Sabbath.

label: Acts 13:43
text: Now when the synagogue broke up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas; who, speaking to them, urged them to continue in the grace of God.

label: Acts 13:44
text: The next Sabbath, almost the whole city was gathered together to hear the word of God.

label: Acts 13:45
text: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with jealousy, and contradicted the things which were spoken by Paul, and blasphemed.

label: Acts 13:46
text: Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly, and said, “It was necessary that God’s word should be spoken to you first. Since indeed you thrust it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles.

label: Acts 13:47
text:
For so has the Lord commanded us, saying,
‘I have set you as a light for the Gentiles,
that you should bring salvation to the uttermost parts of the earth.’”

label: Acts 13:48
text: As the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of God. As many as were appointed to eternal life believed.

label: Acts 13:49
text: The Lord’s word was spread abroad throughout all the region.

label: Acts 13:50
text: But the Jews stirred up the devout and prominent women and the chief men of the city, and stirred up a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and threw them out of their borders.

label: Acts 13:51
text: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came to Iconium.

label: Acts 13:52
text: The disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

label: Paul (Saul of Tarsus)
note: First mention at Acts 7:58 as the young man at whose feet the witnesses laid their garments; later Acts chapters reuse this node.

label: Barnabas (Joses)
aka: Joseph called Barnabas; 'Son of Encouragement'; a Levite of Cyprus

label: Herod Antipas
aka: Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee and Perea

label: Theodotos inscription (Jerusalem)
date: Herodian or early Roman (1st century BCE-70 CE)
found: 1913-14, by Raymond Weill, Ophel excavations, City of David, Jerusalem

label: Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a)
held_at: Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem

label: Psalm 16:8-11 ('you will not leave my soul in Sheol')
author: David (traditional attribution)

label: Papyrus 45 (P. Chester Beatty I; leaf with Matt 25:41-26:39 in Vienna)
found: Egypt, most likely the Faiyum; purchased in the 1930s by Chester Beatty from an Egyptian book dealer
held_at: Chester Beatty Library, Dublin; one leaf (Matt 25:41-26:39) in the Papyrus Collection of the Austrian National Library, Vienna (Pap. Vindob. G. 31974)

label: Simeon Niger
note: Named among the prophets and teachers of the Antioch assembly (Acts 13:1); no independent source names him.

label: Lucius of Cyrene
note: Named among the prophets and teachers of the Antioch assembly (Acts 13:1); no independent source names him.

label: Manaen the foster-brother of Herod the tetrarch
note: Named among the prophets and teachers of the Antioch assembly (Acts 13:1) as a syntrophos (foster-brother) of Herod Antipas; no independent source names him.

label: John Mark
note: Attendant (hyperetes) of Barnabas and Paul on the first journey (13:5); he departed at Perga and returned to Jerusalem (13:13).

label: Bar-Jesus (Elymas) the sorcerer
note: A Jewish false prophet and sorcerer at Paphos (13:6); 'Elymas' is given as the interpretation of his name (13:8). No source outside Acts names him.

label: Sergius Paulus, proconsul of Cyprus
note: The proconsul at Paphos, 'a man of understanding' (13:7). The Roman inscriptions naming Sergii Paulli are linked to him only conjecturally; see the attests notes.

label: Perga (Perge)
modern_name: Perge, near Aksu, Antalya Province, Turkey

label: Iconium
note: City of Lycaonia/Phrygia; the brothers here also testified for Timothy (Acts 16:2).

label: Salamis, Cyprus (excavated city)
excavators: Cyprus Exploration Fund (late 19th c.); 1952-1974 campaigns; Department of Antiquities of Cyprus
note: Excavated; finds in the British Museum and the Saint Barnabas monastery collection; international excavations halted after 1974.

label: Nea Paphos (Paphos Archaeological Park)
periods: Hellenistic (c. 300 BCE) to Roman and later
note: Excavated harbour city with the Houses of Dionysos, Orpheus, Aion and Theseus, an agora, an Asklepion, a theatre and the Tombs of the Kings; the Roman provincial capital.

label: Antioch of Pisidia ruins near Yalvaç
excavators: Ramsay and Calder/Hardie surveys and Princeton-supported excavations, 1912-1914 (fetched Wikipedia Antioch of Pisidia article)
periods: Hellenistic (3rd century BC) to Byzantine (fetched Wikipedia Antioch of Pisidia article)

label: Perga (Perge) excavated ruins
periods: Early Bronze Age to Middle Ages (fetched Wikipedia Perga article)

label: Seleucia in Pieria (excavated remains)
periods: Hellenistic to Roman and late antique
note: Hellenistic town, the seaport of Antioch ad Orontes; inner and outer Roman harbours; today in ruins.

label: Claudian boundary stone of L. Sergius Paulus (curator of the Tiber), Rome
note: Records the appointment of the Curators of the banks and the channel of the river Tiber, one of whom was Sergius; an ex-consul. Its identification with the proconsul of Cyprus is a conjecture.

label: Soli (Cyprus) inscription mentioning a proconsul Paulus
date: mid-1st century CE or later (Hogarth; Mitford: probably considerably later)
found: 1887, at Soli, Cyprus, by Luigi Palma di Cesnola
note: Mentions a proconsul Paulus; Mitford argued on epigraphic grounds that it cannot be dated earlier than the mid-1st century and is probably considerably later, weakening the identification.

label: Miletus theatre inscription, 'Place of the Jews who are also (called) God-fearers' (CIJ 748)
note: A reserved-seat inscription in the Miletus theatre for Jews and theosebeis (God-fearers). Later than Acts 13 and from a different province; context evidence only.

label: Cassius Dio, Roman History 54.4.1 (Cyprus and Narbonensis given proconsuls)
author: Cassius Dio

label: Psalm 2:7 ('You are my son. Today I have become your father.')
author: Psalmist

label: Habakkuk 1:5 ('I am working a work in your days')
author: Habakkuk (traditional attribution)

label: 1 Samuel 13:14 ('a man after his own heart')
author: Deuteronomistic historian (traditional attribution)

label: The Antioch assembly had prophets and teachers
statement: The assembly at Antioch had prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen the foster-brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

label: Fasting, prayer and laying on of hands at a commissioning
statement: After fasting and prayer the Antioch prophets and teachers laid their hands on Barnabas and Saul and sent them away, as the Holy Spirit had directed.

label: Barnabas and Saul sailed from Seleucia to Cyprus
statement: Sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia and from there sailed to Cyprus.

label: They proclaimed God's word in the Jewish synagogues of Salamis
statement: At Salamis in Cyprus they proclaimed God's word in the Jewish synagogues of the city.

label: John (Mark) was their attendant
statement: They had John (John Mark) as their attendant (hyperetes) on Cyprus.

label: Bar-Jesus, a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet, was at Paphos with the proconsul
statement: At Paphos they found a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus, who was with the proconsul and withstood them, seeking to turn the proconsul from the faith; 'Elymas' is given as the interpretation of his name.

label: Sergius Paulus was proconsul of Cyprus
statement: Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding, held the office of proconsul of Cyprus and summoned Barnabas and Saul to hear the word of God.

label: Cyprus was a senatorial province governed by a proconsul
statement: Cyprus was governed by a proconsul, i.e. a senatorial (public) province, not an imperial one.

label: Saul is here also called Paul
statement: The narrative first gives Saul's Roman-style name: 'Saul, who is also called Paul', filled with the Holy Spirit.

label: Elymas was struck blind for a season
statement: Paul announced that the hand of the Lord was on Elymas; immediately a mist and darkness fell on him and he went about seeking someone to lead him by the hand. (Miracle claim.)

label: The proconsul believed when he saw what was done
statement: The proconsul, seeing what was done, believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.

label: They sailed from Paphos to Perga in Pamphylia
statement: Paul and his company set sail from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia.

label: John Mark departed at Perga and returned to Jerusalem
statement: John (Mark) departed from them at Perga and returned to Jerusalem; the reason is not given.

label: They entered the synagogue of Antioch of Pisidia on the Sabbath
statement: Passing on from Perga they came to Antioch of Pisidia and went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day and sat down.

label: Sabbath synagogue service: reading of Law and Prophets, then an invitation to speak
statement: After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent word inviting anyone with a word of exhortation to speak.

label: Gentile God-fearers attended diaspora synagogue services
statement: Paul addresses 'Men of Israel, and you who fear God' (and again at v. 26): Gentile sympathizers with Judaism sat in the diaspora synagogue alongside Jews.

label: God raised up David as king, 'a man after my heart'
statement: In the speech's retelling, God removed Saul and raised up David, testifying 'I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who will do all my will.' (Biblical retelling; cross-reference.)

label: They found no cause for death yet asked Pilate to have him killed
statement: The rulers of Jerusalem, finding no cause of death in Jesus, still asked Pilate to have him killed.

label: They took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb
statement: When they had fulfilled all that was written of him, they took Jesus down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.

label: He was seen many days by those who came up from Galilee to Jerusalem
statement: God raised Jesus from the dead, and he was seen for many days by those who came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are his witnesses. (Appearance claim.)

label: Paul quoted Psalm 2:7 of the resurrection
statement: In the speech, the raising of Jesus fulfils what is 'written in the second psalm: You are my Son. Today I have become your father.'

label: Paul quoted Isaiah 55:3 ('the sure mercies of David')
statement: Paul cites Isaiah: 'I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David' (Isaiah 55:3) of the resurrection, 'no more to return to corruption'.

label: Paul quoted Psalm 16:10 ('you will not allow your Holy One to see decay')
statement: Paul cites 'another psalm': 'You will not allow your Holy One to see decay' (Psalm 16:10), and argues David saw decay but the raised one did not (vv. 36-37).

label: Paul quoted Habakkuk 1:5 as a warning
statement: The speech closes with the prophets' warning: 'Behold, you scoffers, and wonder, and perish; for I work a work in your days...' (Habakkuk 1:5).

label: Devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas
statement: When the synagogue broke up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas.

label: Paul applied Isaiah 49:6 to the mission to the Gentiles
statement: Paul and Barnabas say the Lord commanded them: 'I have set you as a light for the Gentiles, that you should bring salvation to the uttermost parts of the earth' (Isaiah 49:6).

label: The Jews stirred up the city's notables and expelled Paul and Barnabas
statement: The Jews stirred up the devout and prominent women and the chief men of the city, raised a persecution and threw Paul and Barnabas out of their borders.

label: They shook off the dust of their feet against the city
statement: Paul and Barnabas shook off the dust of their feet against the persecutors and came to Iconium.

label: They came to Iconium from Pisidian Antioch
statement: Shaking off the dust of their feet, they came to Iconium, the next city on the route east.
